brief.recommendation: The root blocker has been idle for 21.6s. Revenue at risk is $13,340/min. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout. Waiting 60s would accumulate $799,800 in lost revenue against a $13,340/min cost of interruption. The trade-off EXCEEDS the tolerated degradation.

audit.report: The adhoc_reporting batch_worker session (pid 1661831) opened a transaction and became idle, blocking checkouts for over 21 seconds. The blocker accumulated 21.6s of idle time, during which checkout success dropped to 28% and revenue fell to ~$13,340/min at risk. Both guardians confirmed the blocker was within the 60s business tolerance for degraded checkout and that terminating it risked interrupting an unregistered batch workload with unknown interruption cost. After three rounds of negotiation, the guardians could not reach agreement and escalated to an on-call.
audit.root_cause: An idle batch_worker/adhoc_reporting transaction (pid 1661831) held a lock that blocked checkout sessions, and the workload was absent from the registry, preventing cost-aware termination decisions.
lessons: Register adhoc_reporting in biz.workload_registry immediately so future negotiations can quantify interruption cost and avoid risky terminations.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians correctly prioritized waiting given the blocker's 21.6s age and the 60s tolerance, but the continuity_guardian's invariant override incorrectly modeled the revenue-at-risk calculation, and the database_guardian did not surface the missing workload registry entry until after the escalation.
follow_ups: Add adhoc_reporting to the workload registry with owner and cost fields.
Implement automatic abort for idle-in-transaction sessions exceeding 10s.
Review and document any protected-class status for adhoc_reporting before the next incident.
